subject: Dedicated capacity integration follow-up: SDK/auth/routing + autoscaling sizing
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Samir Gupta <samir@brightpay.com>, Priya Rao <priya@brightpay.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity integration follow-up: SDK/auth/routing + autoscaling sizing

Hi Samir / Priya —

Great to chat today. Quick recap from our discovery and the integration/architecture items we discussed. I want to make sure we’re aligned on next steps and the data points Aditya needs to finalize a sizing recommendation.

Key asks / summary:
- Integration surface
  - SDKs: Python + Node quickstart available; we support direct REST + SDK wrappers.
  - Auth: options are API keys for hosted, mTLS or Okta SSO for control-plane in Private/Dedicated. Please confirm your SSO provider (Okta?) and whether you prefer service-account API keys for the app tier.
  - Routing: you can pin customers to regional pools or model variants. We recommend model pinning for reranker/embedding flows to guarantee deterministic latency.

- Structured output & tool calling
  - We support function/tool calling and structured JSON output via the SDK. If you need schema enforcement we can include a post-processing hook at the edge.

- Embeddings + reranker pattern
  - Typical approach: embeddings are generated via a dedicated embeddings endpoint (batching configurable). Vector store (customer-managed or Redwood-managed) + lightweight reranker call to a low-latency model variant.
  - We recommend batching embeddings to 16–64 per request for throughput. Reranker queries should be routed to a model variant with reduced context size for lower cost/latency.

- Throughput / concurrency numbers we discussed (please verify):
  - Expected steady-state: ~50 rps (3000 rpm) for user-facing generation flows.
  - Peak bursts: up to 200–250 rps for short windows (holiday/promo).
  - Average tokens per generation request: ~800 tokens.
  - Embeddings: ~32 items per batch during offline indexing windows.

- Dedicated capacity sizing considerations (high-level)
  - Baseline pool: 4 GPUs (balanced) + autoscale to 8 GPUs for bursts; concurrency per-GPU estimated at 6 concurrent short requests (varies by model/quantization).
  - Queueing: recommend a FIFO queue with a short interactive priority lane for user requests and a lower-priority batch lane for bulk embeddings/cron jobs.
  - Autoscale policy: aggressive scaling for burst tolerance (scale-up on queued requests > X), scale-down with a cool-down.

Next steps / asks for you:
1) Confirm SSO provider (Okta) and whether you need SAML-only or SAML + SCIM for provisioning.
2) Provide a 24h/day peak sample (one day of traffic) if possible or representative QPS numbers per route (generate, embed, rerank).
3) Confirm whether the vector store will be customer-hosted or Redwood-managed.

I'll attach a short proposal and our SDK quickstart. Aditya will take the lead on sizing once we have the confirmed QPS/tokens. Can we schedule a 30-min technical sync with your infra/infra-security folks next week?

Thanks —
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0198

Attachments: brightpay-dedicated-proposal.pdf (proposal stub), redwood-quickstart-sdk-guide.zip (SDK quickstart archive)

From: Samir Gupta <samir@brightpay.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya@brightpay.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Jul 2026 09:14:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity integration follow-up: SDK/auth/routing + autoscaling sizing

Thanks Marissa — very helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- Okta is our IdP (SAML + SCIM for provisioning would be ideal). We also have a short-lived-service-account workflow for backend-to-backend calls. How do you recommend combining those?
- Traffic numbers: steady-state closer to 120 reqs/min for generation (2 rps), but peak marketing-driven bursts could approach 420 rps for a few minutes. Embeddings workload: nightly batch windows, ~10k items per night, prefer batching of 32.
- Average tokens per request is closer to 900–1,200 for some of our longer churn-analysis prompts.

Two asks: can you provide the short SOC2/CD documentation and a proposed SLA for Dedicated? Also—does Redwood support IAM role-based access to the Dedicated control plane (so we can grant the infra team limited permissions)?

We’re keen to get a sizing proposal and a Statement of Work. Happy to block the 30-min tech sync next Tue or Wed (UTC-7) — Priya will coordinate.

—Samir
Samir Gupta
Head of Platform Engineering, BrightPay
samir@brightpay.com

On Tue, Jul 28, 2026 at 4:02 PM Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com> wrote:
> (See recap below)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Samir Gupta <samir@brightpay.com>, Priya Rao <priya@brightpay.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Jul 2026 11:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity integration follow-up: SDK/auth/routing + autoscaling sizing

Thanks Samir — appreciate the traffic details. Answers inline + next steps: 

- Okta + SCIM: we support SAML SSO for the control plane & SCIM for provisioning user accounts. For service-to-service calls you can use short-lived API keys minted by the control plane; for on-prem/private deployments we support mTLS for node-to-node auth. We also offer role-based access controls and can integrate with your IdP for RBAC mappings.

- Tokens: 900–1,200 average changes concurrency/throughput assumptions. With ~1,000 tokens/request we’d model lower qps per GPU; I’ll have Aditya run the exact capacity calc.

- IAM roles: Redwood Dedicated supports role-based access on the control plane; infra can be given a limited admin scope. We’ll include that in the SOW.

Sizing recommendation (preliminary):
- Baseline pool: 8 GPUs (N baseline) to provide buffer for longer prompts.
- Max pool: 16 GPUs for autoscale (burst headroom given your 420 rps peaks).
- Concurrency: start with 6–8 concurrent slots per GPU for long-prompt workloads; we can tune after a week of traffic.
- Queueing: implement two queues — interactive (priority, low-latency) and batch (batch embeddings, low priority).

Attachments and links:
- Proposal: brightpay-dedicated-proposal.pdf (attached) — includes SOW draft, SLA, and pricing ranges.
- SDK quickstart: redwood-quickstart-sdk-guide.zip (attached) — examples for Python/Node auth flows and routing.
- HubSpot: HS-98234 (I added the deal record and initial SOW there).
- Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-brightpay (architecture diagrams + example configs).

Next steps:
1) Priya / Samir: confirm Tue/Wed availability for a 30-min tech sync.
2) Samir: confirm whether vector store will be customer-hosted or Redwood-managed.
3) Aditya: will follow up with a detailed GPU sizing calc and sample autoscale policy.

I’ll also include SOC2 artifacts in a separate secure link once procurement confirms the NDA flow.

Thank you —
Marissa

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Jul 2026 15:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity integration follow-up: SDK/auth/routing + autoscaling sizing

Marissa — short internal note following their numbers. I’ll prepare the sizing calc and an autoscale policy draft. Initial thoughts: 

- Given 420 rps short bursts and ~1k tokens/request, 8 baseline GPUs may still be tight depending on model; I recommend modeling with 6 baseline + ability to scale to 12–16. I’ll produce two scenarios (cost-optimized + performance-optimized).
- Concurrency: assume 4–6 concurrent heavy slots per GPU for long-context prompts; we can increase concurrency for smaller responses.
- Queueing: implement token-aware queue throttling (limit inflight tokens) plus priority lane for interactive.

I’ll attach the calc and send by EOD Monday. If you want I can join the tech sync to cover kernel/quantization tradeoffs.

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com
